top_choice_rationale: The GLP-1 arc is mature and independently confirmed in large randomized trials, so an award is clearly warranted. I rank Drucker, Holst and Mojsov first because a discovery citation maps three distinct, necessary steps: human physiology and secretion (Holst), receptor biology and proglucagon-derived peptides (Drucker), and identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) form (Mojsov). The therapeutic payoff is named as a consequence of the discovery rather than as a separately credited achievement. The main weakness is Mojsov's priority relative to the Habener group, which I cannot resolve from the supplied material. If the primary record showed her contribution to be inseparable from that group's, I would move to the Drucker, Holst and Knudsen trio, which is my second choice and clearly preferable to no award.
